lesson_title: The Line at the Bottom of the Slip: VAT
hook_text: The VAT on your slip? The shop never keeps a cent of it.
clip_script: Look at the bottom of any till slip. There's a line marked VAT. You paid it — nobody asked you. And here's what surprises people: the shop doesn't keep it. The shop is a collector, not an owner. It takes that money at the till, holds it, and hands it to SARS. Now the sum everybody gets wrong. A slip says R2 300 including VAT — how much VAT is inside? Almost everyone takes fifteen percent of R2 300 and gets R345. Wrong. The fifteen percent was worked out on the SMALLER number, the price before tax. R2 300 is already the whole thing: a hundred parts of price plus fifteen parts of tax — a hundred and fifteen parts. So the tax is fifteen parts out of a hundred and fifteen: R300. Going up, fifteen on a hundred. Coming down, fifteen on a hundred and fifteen. And that money in the till? Trust money — it was never the shop's to spend.
visual_style: A till slip filling the frame, the VAT line glowing; a wrong calculation flashing red and cancelling; a bar splitting into 100 blue parts and 15 gold parts to show the 15/115 logic; coins moving from the till into a SARS strongbox.
pacing: Slip reveal, myth-bust beat, clear visual derivation, slogan landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never lose a VAT mark again.
